course.title: Distributed Observability & Telemetry Engineering
course.tagline: Design low-cardinality metrics, structured traces, and SLO burn alerts that survive overload.
about: Observability is not collecting every log line; it is instrumenting the exact signals required to isolate failure modes under time pressure.
In this course you design telemetry schemas, bound label cardinality, and derive multi-window SLO burn alerts.
outcomes: Bound telemetry cardinality so monitoring never collapses during traffic spikes.
Translate user-facing reliability requirements into SLI formulas and multi-window burn alerts.
Correlate distributed traces with structured redacted logs using request IDs.
course.artifact: A production observability design doc + SLO burn-rate specification for a multi-service checkout path.

competencies.title: Observability & SLO Telemetry
competencies.blurb: Design bounded-cardinality metrics, correlated traces, and error-budget burn alerts.
competencies.definition: Architect operational telemetry pipelines that expose leading indicators of degradation without introducing unbounded cardinality or PII leakage.

frameworkAnchors.note: Continuous technical performance measurement and operational monitoring.

levelDescriptors.observableOutcome: Distinguish SLIs, SLOs, and SLAs and identify unbounded label cardinality hazards.
Explain why multi-window error-budget burn alerts outperform static threshold alerts.
Design a redacted telemetry pipeline with latency histograms and request correlation.
Ship a complete observability & runbook specification validated against overload scenarios.

modules.title: Telemetry Foundations & Cardinality
modules.summary: Separate high-signal operational metrics from noisy debug exhaust.

lessons.title: Bounded Cardinality & Secret Redaction
lessons.summary: Why putting user IDs in Prometheus labels takes down monitoring during incidents.
keep: Never put unbounded identifiers (userId, requestId, email) in metric labels.
Put high-cardinality correlation IDs in structured logs and traces with automatic PII redaction.

blocks.text: Every unique combination of metric label values creates a distinct time series in memory. Putting a user ID or raw URL path into a metric label multiplies memory usage linearly with traffic—meaning your monitoring fails right when an incident spikes.

blocks.title: Rule of Thumb
blocks.text: Metrics stay low-cardinality (route template, status class, operation name). Logs and distributed traces carry X-Request-Id and hashed actor references.

blocks.q: Which label is safe to attach to an HTTP request latency histogram metric?
options: The full URL including query parameters
The normalized route template and HTTP status class (e.g. /paths/$slug, 2xx)
blocks.why: Normalized route templates and status classes have a small, fixed set of values (low cardinality), preventing time-series explosion while preserving actionable latency breakdowns.

labs.title: Multi-Window SLO Burn Alert & Redaction Design
labs.brief: Define SLIs, a 30-day error budget, multi-window burn-rate alerts, and a log-redaction policy for a user-facing API.
steps: Specify the exact good-events / valid-events SLI ratio for availability and p95 latency.
Calculate the 30-day error budget minutes for a 99.9% SLO.
Define fast-burn (2% budget in 1h) and slow-burn (5% budget in 6h) alert rules with linked runbooks.
List every field that must be redacted before logs leave the server.
labs.twist: A client bug sends 20,000 malformed 400 Bad Request calls per minute—ensure your SLI excludes client-side 4xx errors without hiding genuine 5xx outages.
labs.artifact: A structured SLO + redaction specification document with worked burn-rate math.

rubric.labTitle: Multi-Window SLO Burn Alert & Redaction Design

criteria.label: SLI Formula & Error Budget Arithmetic
criteria.rationale: Ambiguous SLI definitions produce noisy alerts and broken error budgets.
criteria.evidenceRequired: Exact numerator/denominator formula plus worked 30-day downtime budget.
typicalFailureModes: Counting 4xx client errors as server availability failures

descriptors.1: SLI or error budget omitted or incorrect.
descriptors.2: SLI stated informally without exact numerator/denominator or budget math.
descriptors.3: Exact SLI ratio and 30-day error budget arithmetic clearly verified.
descriptors.4: SLI handles edge cases (4xx exclusion, health probes) with sensitivity bounds.

criteria.revisionHint: Write out good/valid event definitions and show the exact minutes in a 30-day 99.9% budget.

criteria.label: Multi-Window Burn-Rate Alerting
criteria.rationale: Single-window thresholds either alert too slowly or page on brief blips.
criteria.evidenceRequired: Fast and slow burn windows with explicit page vs. ticket routing.
typicalFailureModes: Paging on 1-minute CPU spikes instead of user-visible error burn

descriptors.1: Only static host CPU/memory alerts provided.
descriptors.2: Burn rate mentioned without short/long confirmation windows.
descriptors.3: Fast-burn page and slow-burn ticket windows specified with runbook triggers.
descriptors.4: Dual-window burn rates verified for detection time and reset time under burst load.

criteria.revisionHint: Pair each long window with a short confirmation window to stop alert flapping.

criteria.label: Telemetry Privacy & Cardinality Hygiene
criteria.rationale: Logs leaking tokens or unbounded metric labels create security and outage incidents.
criteria.evidenceRequired: Redaction denylist and explicit low-cardinality metric label schema.
typicalFailureModes: Logging Authorization headers or raw emails

descriptors.2: General mention of privacy without concrete fields or label bounds.
descriptors.3: Explicit redaction list and bounded metric label set specified.
descriptors.4: Automated test assertions defined to prevent secret leakage and label explosion.

criteria.revisionHint: Enumerate exact sensitive keys to redact and cap metric labels to bounded enums.
